clue.text: Set up raffle for old cold chicken

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
O is a standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a raffle is a prize draw

explanation.surface: Someone rigs a raffle where the prize is a chilled roast chicken past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: The two abbreviations come in the opposite order to the clue, then the upturned raffle word ends COWARD. 'Chicken' looks like the raffle prize but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is informal slang for someone lacking courage, a timid person who runs from danger.

clue.text: A full set of marbles for everyone present

definitions.note: noun phrase for an adjectival answer: having a full set of marbles

parts.note: everyone means all of them
someone present is there

explanation.surface: A teacher hands out a complete set of marbles so every child in the room gets some.
explanation.walkthrough: To have all your marbles is a British idiom for being mentally sound; the clue's marbles are not toys.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all there is an idiom for being sane and alert, just as having your full set of marbles means.

clue.text: Move to avoid delivery of ball, securing wide

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: in tennis the delivery of the ball is the serve
W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A batsman dodges a wayward delivery that goes wide of the stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of balls and wides hides a tennis serve; W for wide comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve is to change direction suddenly so as to dodge an obstacle or collision.

clue.text: Police officer gets one chance to be the captain assistant

parts.note: cop is slang for a police officer
the Roman numeral for one
a lot is something decided by chance, as in drawing lots

explanation.surface: A police officer is given a single opportunity to serve as the captain's assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-pilot is the second pilot who assists the captain in flying an aircraft.

clue.text: Not divulging information about purpose of cultural institution

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to keep mum is to say nothing
the use of a thing is its purpose

explanation.surface: A cultural institution refuses to reveal what it is actually for.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum is a public institution that keeps and displays objects of cultural, historical or scientific interest.

clue.text: Get material for the Opposition leader close to election

parts.note: cotton is a woven fabric

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

indicators.note: the close of something is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone fetches fabric for the opposition leader's campaign as an election approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' reads as fetch, but it is the definition in the sense of understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is an informal phrasal verb meaning to understand or grasp something at last.

clue.text: Lad taking £2 to join club for film-makers

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it, so the money sits inside the lad

parts.note: a lad is a boy
L is the abbreviation for a pound, so two pounds is two Ls
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A young man pays two pounds to become a member of a film club.
explanation.walkthrough: L for pound comes from the Latin libra; a wood is a long-distance golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Bollywood is the Hindi-language film industry based in Mumbai, its studios collectively being film-makers.

clue.text: Castrated animal returned with buttocks round, plump and comely

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: bum is British slang for the buttocks

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an ox is a castrated bull

explanation.surface: A gelded beast comes back with a well-rounded rump, looking plump and attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Buxom describes a woman who is attractively full-figured, plump and healthy-looking.

clue.text: Purgative for use when badly cooked roast contributes to wind

indicators.note: contributing to something means going into it, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to wind is to coil

indicators.note: something badly cooked comes out a mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A laxative recommended after a badly cooked roast has caused flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' suggests flatulence, but it is the verb meaning to coil.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor oil is a traditional laxative, a medicine that purges the bowels.

clue.text: Greek letter written backwards in fat ledger

indicators.note: writing backwards puts the letters in right-to-left order
in says the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters sit across the two words

explanation.surface: A Greek character has been scrawled back to front in a thick account book.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, written as a triangle in capital form.

clue.text: Working at Foreign Office intelligence

parts.note: someone working at a place is in there, on duty
FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office, the British government department

explanation.surface: A spy has a job at the Foreign Office gathering intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' suggests spies, but here it just means facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is a clipped form of information, and intelligence also means information or news.

clue.text: Failing head about to get stick

indicators.note: something failing breaks down and falls apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A headteacher who is not up to the job is about to be beaten with a cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a noun, the cane, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or be fixed firmly to a surface, as glue does.

clue.text: Soothing cream prescribed during appointments

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the letters lie inside the next word

parts.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: A doctor writes a prescription for a soothing cream at a consultation.
explanation.definitionFit: An ointment is a smooth greasy preparation rubbed on the skin to heal or soothe it.

clue.text: Shoulder to shoulder, as sailor takes his last bearing

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
the last letter of the sailor named just before
east is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Sailors standing side by side as one of them takes a final compass reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' points back to the word sailor, whose final letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Abreast means side by side, level with one another, facing the same way.

clue.text: Traded on behalf of others without money to get wine?

parts.note: someone broke has no money
red is red wine

explanation.surface: A penniless agent wonders if acting for clients might earn a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To broker is to act as an intermediary, arranging deals and trades for other people.

clue.text: Oils processed in large farm container

indicators.note: processing transforms raw material, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Refined oils are stored in a big tank on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a tall tower or pit on a farm used to store grain or fodder.

clue.text: Sweet affectionate creature

parts.note: to be fond is to be affectionate
an ant is a small creature

explanation.surface: A description of a cute and loving animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as an adjective describing the creature, but it is the noun, a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft sugar paste used as a confectionery filling or cake icing.

clue.text: Lonely miss stood up during tryst

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tryst is a romantic date

indicators.note: in a down clue, something stood up is raised to read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to miss a chance is to lose it

explanation.surface: A young woman left alone after her date failed to show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' and 'stood up' suggest a jilted young woman; really the first is a verb and the second turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate means bleakly empty and forlorn, feeling abandoned and alone.

clue.text: Riches spread about to trap a person with access to the till

definitions.text: a person with access to the till

indicators.note: trapping something holds it inside, so one piece encloses the other
spreading things about scatters them, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wealth is scattered about to lure in someone who can get at the cash register.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashier works at a shop counter or bank, handling the money in the register.

clue.text: Trot about visiting sick with a savoury pancake

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
sick means ill
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hurries round to see an invalid, bringing a savoury pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flat Mexican flatbread of maize or wheat, a kind of savoury pancake.

clue.text: How to save money for plant?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: careful, economical use of money
second meaning: a pink-flowered coastal plant, also called sea pink

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'plant' is not a factory or a spy but a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift is frugality, the habit of saving; it is also the name of a low cushion-forming seaside flower.

clue.text: A bit of a fry up is not so wise

definitions.text: A bit of a fry up
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a slice of bacon, one part of a cooked breakfast
second meaning: more reckless, the comparative of an adjective for hasty

explanation.walkthrough: A fry-up is a British cooked breakfast of eggs, bacon, sausages and the like; a rasher is a slice of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a thin slice of bacon, and more rash means more reckless, less sensible.

clue.text: Another chance to watch priest taking part in race

indicators.note: taking part in something puts you inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a relay is a team race
P is an abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: Viewers want to see again the moment a clergyman joined a charity race.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay is a repeated showing of a recorded event, letting viewers see it once more.

clue.text: Book set in West Herefordshire

indicators.note: something set in a place is embedded within it, so the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A novel whose action takes place in the western part of an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Herefordshire is an English county on the Welsh border; the 'Book' is biblical rather than a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a book of the Old Testament, telling of the Jewish queen of Persia.

clue.text: Examined the rabble orally

indicators.note: orally means by mouth, so the word is the one spoken, not written

parts.note: the herd is the common crowd, the rabble

explanation.surface: A mob is given a spoken test, as in an oral exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orally' looks like part of an exam scene but signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that has heard a case has examined it, listening to the evidence and argument.

clue.text: Fried potato cooked a lot with a sausage

parts.note: a chip is a fried strip of potato

indicators.note: cooking changes the ingredients, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plate of chips, cooked in quantity, served alongside a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage, common in Britain with roasts and breakfasts.

clue.text: Stocky social worker's extremely friendly

parts.note: a worker bee belongs to a social colony

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so just the first and last letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A burly social worker who is very friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' reads as a care professional, but it is a worker bee, an insect living in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy means muscular and solidly built, as stocky means short and sturdy.

clue.text: Fines, which are taken on the spot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: punishments, often sums of money

definitions.text: which are taken on the spot
definitions.meaning: second meaning: football kicks taken from the penalty spot

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the spot' suggests on-the-spot fines, but the second meaning is the football penalty spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Penalties are punishments such as fines, and in football they are kicks taken from a marked spot.
